declaration.negotiation_history_statement: As interim class counsel, I support preliminary approval. The parties reached this settlement through three rounds of arm’s-length negotiations after the complaint survived a motion to dismiss and before class certification. Class relief and attorneys’ fees were discussed together from the outset; I do not represent that fees were first discussed only after class relief was agreed. As negotiations progressed, the fee amount remained unchanged while proposed relief to class members increased. The resulting agreement provides a $34 million class fund, with payments made automatically to identified members without a claim form, and up to $6 million in separately paid fees and expenses, subject to court approval. Brightline retains the right to address the fee request, and any fees not awarded will go to the class rather than revert to Brightline. In my judgment, the settlement is fair, reasonable, and adequate for preliminary-approval purposes: the fund represents approximately 53% of the $64 million in disputed charges, provides relief without the delay and uncertainty of litigation, and avoids substantial certification and trial risks. The fee request remains subject to the Court’s independent review.

backchannel.speaker: plaintiff
backchannel.message: We are open to an early resolution that delivers substantial, automatic payments to identified members. Any fee request must be reasonable and subject to court approval, and any fees not awarded should benefit the class rather than revert to Brightline. Please let me know whether those principles provide a basis for a term sheet.

backchannel.speaker: defense
backchannel.message: Yes, those principles provide a basis for discussion. We are prepared to explore automatic payments to identified members, a court-reviewed fee request, and allocation of any unawarded fees to the class. The fund and fee amounts remain to be negotiated.

backchannel.speaker: plaintiff
backchannel.message: We have a basis to move forward. Please put forward a complete term sheet with a substantial class fund, automatic payments to all identified members, a reasonable court-approved fee paid separately, and any unawarded fees going to the class. Concrete numbers would help us assess whether an early resolution is possible.

backchannel.speaker: defense
backchannel.message: Here is a concrete starting point for a complete term sheet: $28 million class fund, $6 million in separately paid attorneys’ fees and expenses subject to court approval, automatic payments to all identified members, no clear-sailing agreement, and any unawarded fees added to the class fund rather than returned to Brightline. Total cash outlay would be $34 million. Would that provide a basis for an on-record proposal?

backchannel.speaker: plaintiff
backchannel.message: Your proposal is a constructive starting point, particularly the automatic distribution and allocation of any unawarded fees to the class. We cannot support a $28 million class fund at this stage. Would Brightline consider a $36 million class fund and $7 million in separately paid, court-approved fees and expenses, with the other terms as you proposed?

backchannel.speaker: defense
backchannel.message: We appreciate the movement, but $36 million for the class plus $7 million in fees is beyond what we can offer. Could we bridge the gap at a $33 million class fund and $6 million in separately paid, court-approved fees and expenses? Distribution would be automatic, there would be no clear-sailing agreement, and any unawarded fees would go to the class.
